revolta.title: ReVolta PR #59: SM70 score multi-request decode batches by request segments
revolta.idea: group query rows of one request into a segment so a paged QSA scorer loads each key tile once per segment; up to four rows, FP16 H4/D128, int32 metadata, device-built segment descriptors, CUDA-graph safe; single-row-per-request batches keep the paged scorer.
revolta.reported_measurement: 4 x V100 PCIe at 250 W; decode throughput on/off 1.01-1.24 across DFlash2/MTP4 shapes; C1 unchanged; run-to-run divergence at 4-8 requests.

strata.change: STRATA_QSA_SEGMENTS groups contiguous rows of one slot in a --batch-mtp verify window; STRATA_BATCH_VERIFY_WIDTH widens a slot group to the row budget. Both are opt-in and change no default.
strata.difference: Strata reuses its existing int8/fp16 multi-row QSA calls in the batch-MTP verifier and requires bitwise equality; ReVolta changes a vLLM SM70 paged scorer for arbitrary request segments. The engines, models, KV formats and power caps differ, so throughput is not directly comparable.

texts: Write a complete, production-quality Python module that merges overlapping half-open intervals. Include the full implementation with type hints and docstrings, a comprehensive test suite covering empty input, touching intervals, nested intervals, invalid bounds and very large inputs, and a short design/complexity discussion. Target at least 1000 words; do not stop early.

Write a complete C++17 CSV line parser that handles quoted fields, escaped quotes and embedded newlines. Provide the full implementation, a comprehensive test suite with edge cases, the build command, and a short discussion of the state machine and complexity. Target at least 1000 words; do not stop early.

Write a complete Rust library that validates balanced brackets and reports the exact error position. Include the full implementation, a comprehensive test suite with malformed and valid inputs, property-style cases, and a design/complexity discussion. Target at least 1000 words; do not stop early.

Write a complete Go implementation of a bounded-concurrency URL worker pool with cancellation and backpressure. Include the full implementation, a comprehensive test suite with a fake fetcher, race-safe tests, and a detailed explanation of shutdown and error propagation. Target at least 1000 words; do not stop early.

Write a complete TypeScript debounce utility with cancel, flush and leading/trailing options. Include the full implementation, a comprehensive Jest or Vitest test suite with fake timers, and a detailed explanation of timer ownership and `this` typing. Target at least 1000 words; do not stop early.

Write a complete Python B-tree implementation with insert, search, delete and range scan. Include the full implementation, a comprehensive test suite comparing against a reference sorted list, and a detailed explanation of node splitting, rebalancing and complexity. Target at least 1000 words; do not stop early.

Write a complete C implementation of a bounds-checked string builder and a small ring buffer. Include the full implementation, a comprehensive test suite covering overflow, truncation, aliasing and allocation failure, and a discussion of the ownership contract. Target at least 1000 words; do not stop early.

Write a complete Python implementation of a transactional in-memory key-value store with snapshots and rollback. Include the full implementation, a comprehensive test suite with nested transactions and failure injection, and a detailed design/complexity discussion. Target at least 1000 words; do not stop early.

code_tasks: Write a Python function `merge_intervals(intervals)` that merges overlapping half-open intervals. Then explain the algorithm, its time and space complexity, and two edge cases.
Write a C++17 function that parses one CSV line with quoted fields and escaped quotes. Then explain the state machine and why it is linear.
Write a Rust function that validates a balanced bracket string. Then explain the stack invariant, the error type you chose, and the complexity.
Write a Python asyncio worker pool that processes a list of URLs with at most N concurrent tasks. Then explain cancellation, backpressure and exception propagation.
Write a SQL query that finds the second-highest salary per department, then explain the window function, ties, and how an index changes the plan.
Write a Go function that detects a cycle in a directed graph. Then explain DFS colours, complexity, and why the recursion depth matters.
Write a JavaScript debounce with a cancel method. Then explain timers, `this`, and the difference from throttle.
Write a C function that copies a NUL-terminated string with explicit bounds checking. Then explain overlap, truncation, and the return convention.

findings.claim: At 262144, two unstreamed batch-MTP slots leave 658 CUDA1 expert-cache slots; one serial slot leaves 4758. KV streaming at two slots restores 3932 while retaining 262144.

Nonce-prompt C1 only: B decode is lower in all four same-round pairs, B/A 0.8367, 0.8574, 0.9282 and 0.8388 (range 0.837-0.928, median 0.848; 7.2-16.3% lower, median 15.2%). Wall range 0.859-1.011 is confounded by A2 output lengths 176/169 versus B 256. This is not the final verdict; the final plain full C1 is +7.4% median.
Nonce-prompt C2 only: full ratios span 0.681-1.376; tokens A 312/512/512/512 and B 512/512/512/275. Short C2 spans 0.941-1.791; two A rounds are 19-token nonce echoes. No throughput claim.

Nonce-prompt C4 only: full favors B in all four same-round pairs (decode 1.118-1.297, median 1.177); short favors B in all four (decode 1.119-1.448, median 1.292) but B has more output in every round. Four pairs are not independent; not proven.

Plain-prompt short-context A/S: C1 S/A wall 1.048 and 1.092, but C1 is not credited to segments; C2 S/A 0.912 and 1.167; C4 1.078 and 0.992 (S1 r0 = 799 tokens). Mixed signs; no consistent STRATA_QSA_SEGMENTS gain.

Final plain full C2 is the strongest positive signal: B is higher in all four same-round pairs, median +13.5%, but one pair is near-neutral and the sample is two repeats. Full C4 also favors B in all four, with one A round at 858 tokens. Full C1 is +7.4% median but not attributed to segments. Short C2 is neutral/slower; short C4 is small and EOS-confounded. Full mode streams KV, so full-mode changes are not segments-only effects. No general gain is proven.

Serial 262144 (parallel 1, no KV stream) vs stream A/B on the same binary, all four rounds: C1 48.92/41.12/44.36; C2 50.97/55.38/62.79. C2 stream B is +13.4% over A and +23.2% over serial by wall; C1 stream B is -9.3% vs serial by wall. Serial ran after A/B, not interleaved. C4 serial 784 vs stream B 1024; do not ratio.
Both switches are opt-in environment variables; no runtime default changed.

answer_outputs.note: The 39-byte answers are exactly the bracketed run/client/round prefix; the model echoed the nonce and stopped at EOS (19 tokens). No semantic quality scoring was done, and no arm-to-arm output equality is claimed.

limitations: n=2 rounds per arm/client. A/B ranges are min/max of four same-round pairs; A/S ranges are min/max of two ratios. None is a confidence interval.
Natural outputs hit EOS before 256 tokens in several rounds; wall tok/s and latency are not comparable across unequal output lengths.
Seven answers are 39-byte nonce echoes; the 19-token outliers are not model answers.
Full mode streams KV; under the streamed cache STRATA_QSA_SEGMENTS groups the indexer append but scores/top-k/attention stay per-row, so the full B arm is not a pure test of the segmented scorer.
The A/B rows compare both switches together; they do not isolate STRATA_QSA_SEGMENTS from STRATA_BATCH_VERIFY_WIDTH.
Kernel parity is not a full serving-correctness claim for the combined flags; wider verify groups can change arithmetic by design.
The baseline is the installed 1b4c32 binary; the captured source baseline is a9e06cb3. No fresh baseline build was run for this report.
Power cap and clocks were not measured; the status power is one aggregate sample for both GPUs, not a controlled power sweep.
HIP was only partially compiled (three host objects); there was no AMD link or runtime. SYCL is a separate implementation and was not built or tested.
Parity covers kernels and captured graphs on sm_70, not full serving under load; no AMD or SYCL parity was exercised.
The nonce A/B HTTP runs used the same run_id and nonce scheme, but not byte-identical outputs; the final plain A/B uses no nonce. No quality or correctness comparison across arms was made.
ReVolta #59 used a different engine, model path and 250 W V100s; its throughput numbers are source claims and are not compared numerically here.
The plain A/S run is n=2 per arm; only one C4 round is short (S1 r0 799 tokens).
Plain-prompt TTFT is a cache-hit time (all but one prompt token cached); it is not a cold-prefill measurement.
Final plain C4 has three short rounds: full A1r0 858, short B1r1 790 and short B2r0 1003. Its C4 ratios are EOS-confounded.
The two serial plain arms ran after the A/B arms, not interleaved. The cross-config comparison has explicit thermal noise and four rounds per level.
C4 is not fixed across paths: serial is 784 in every round, stream A has one 858-token round, and stream B is 1024.
